KinesioCal Privacy Policy

Last updated 11/10/2026

1. Who We Are and Who This Covers

KinesioCal, LLC ("KinesioCal," "we") provides scheduling, booking, client-records, and practice-management software to licensed massage therapists and other service businesses. This policy explains what personal information we collect, how we use it, and the choices you have. It applies to our websites, the KinesioCal application, public booking pages, and our support channels.

Three kinds of people interact with KinesioCal, and your rights depend on which you are:

  • Subscribers and Users — the businesses that pay for KinesioCal and the staff they authorize. We collect your information directly and we decide how it is used; we are the "controller" for it.
  • Clients — members of the public who book or pay for a Subscriber's services. There are two kinds of Client data, with different roles. The business's copy: the business you booked with collects your booking, intake, and treatment records and decides how they are used; KinesioCal processes that copy on the business's behalf as a "processor" or "service provider," and questions about it go to the business. Your own account: if you create a KinesioCal account by claiming your bookings, that account holds your login and your own copy of your contact details, independent of any business. It is not a copy of the business's records: those stay the business's, and you can view and export them from your account but not change or erase them. KinesioCal is the controller of your account and that contact copy, deals with you directly about them, and gives you the notices and rights described in this policy without going through a business.
  • Visitors — anyone who browses our marketing site or contacts us without an account.

Where this policy conflicts with a signed agreement with a Subscriber, the signed agreement controls for that Subscriber's data.

2. Our HIPAA Position

KinesioCal is not currently HIPAA-certified or HIPAA-compliant. We are building the Service with the intent of becoming HIPAA-compliant in the future: the application is designed around the HIPAA Security Rule's administrative, physical, and technical safeguards as a reference standard, but that work is not finished and takes time. We do not represent that the Service currently meets every requirement of the Security Rule, we make no claim that using KinesioCal makes any business HIPAA-compliant, and the safeguards in place may change as the Service develops. We do treat Client data as health information and protect it accordingly, and we never sell personal identifying information or client data (Section 4). As of the date of this policy:

Safeguards in place today

  • connections to the Service are made over HTTPS;
  • role-based access: every staff member holds a role (Owner, Admin, Provider, or a role the business defines) whose permissions the business grants or withholds, and a Provider's view of clients, contact details, notes, and appointments reaches only the clients they have treated;
  • an audit log of who created, changed, downloaded, or exported client records and business data (viewing a record is not logged);
  • a consent record for every record a Client chooses to share from one of their providers to another, listing what was shared and when, which the Client can revoke at any time;
  • minimum-necessary design: every note is marked either shared with the client or staff-only, and staff-only notes never leave the business; exports carry only the records the business holds; and a business can keep the detail in appointment emails to a minimum;
  • separation of each Subscriber's data from every other Subscriber's;
  • automatic session timeouts;
  • strong-password rules on every login: a minimum length, no common, all-number or name-based passwords, and complexity requirements, checked whenever a password is set;
  • encryption at rest: the database, uploaded files, and backups are stored on encrypted storage at our hosting provider, and the most sensitive content, including the notes a Subscriber keeps about a Client, intake answers, connected-calendar credentials, and Safety Network identifiers and review content, is additionally encrypted inside the application before it is stored, so that it is unreadable without the application's own keys;
  • a written security risk assessment and incident-response plan, reviewed at least yearly and after any change to how data is handled.

We will update this list as safeguards are added or change. We do not offer a Business Associate Agreement at this time.

Whether HIPAA applies to a Subscriber depends on that Subscriber's own activities, chiefly whether it transmits health information electronically in connection with insurance billing. Subscribers that are HIPAA covered entities must not store protected health information in KinesioCal; we do not offer HIPAA compliance or a Business Associate Agreement on any plan today, and we will update this policy if that changes.

We do not collect Social Security numbers or tax identification numbers from Clients, Subscribers, or Users.

Cookies and similar technologies. The application sets only the cookies it needs to work: a session cookie that keeps you signed in (it ends after 12 hours, or after 10 minutes without activity) and a security token that protects forms against forgery. Your browser's local storage holds device-level conveniences such as your light or dark theme, a booking you have not finished, and a few view settings; that information stays on your device and is not sent to us. When a card form loads, Stripe sets its own cookies to prevent payment fraud, under Stripe's privacy policy. Our marketing website, the pages you read before signing in or booking, may use Google Analytics to count visits and see which pages are read. Google Analytics sets its own cookies holding a random visitor ID and records the pages you view, your approximate location, and your device and browser type; we run it without Google's advertising features, so it is not used to show you ads or to follow you across other sites, and you can block it with Google's opt-out browser add-on at https://tools.google.com/dlpage/gaoptout. The application itself, including sign-in, booking, the portal, and everything behind them, carries no analytics, advertising cookies, or tracking pixels. Nothing we set requires your consent under United States law, so you will not see a cookie banner.

4. How We Use Information, and What We Will Never Do

We will never sell Client Personal identifying Information (PII) or Health Information. We do not sell, rent, or trade any Client's name, contact details, health information, booking history, or payment information to anyone, for any purpose. We do not share Client information with advertisers or data brokers. We do not train AI or machine-learning models on Client information, and we do not sell, license, or intentionally provide Client information to any AI company or other third party for use as training data. This commitment also applies to Subscriber and User information.

We use information only to:

  • provide the Service: schedule appointments, send confirmations and reminders, store records;
  • send transactional messages on a Subscriber's behalf (reminders, receipts, recapture messages the Subscriber configures);
  • bill Subscribers and prevent fraud;
  • respond to support requests, including with AI-assisted tools (see "How we use AI tools" below);
  • maintain security, investigate violations of our Terms of Service, and comply with law;
  • improve the Service using de-identified, aggregated statistics that cannot be linked to any person or business;
  • send Subscribers product updates, which you can opt out of at any time.

How we use AI tools. KinesioCal is a small company and uses third-party AI services in two ways: to help build and maintain the software, and to help triage, draft, and in some cases respond to support requests and bug reports. Today those services are Claude (Anthropic) and ChatGPT (OpenAI); others may be added. Each runs under its own terms and privacy policy, which we do not control. We take the following steps to limit what those services receive:

  • We review each AI provider's published terms before using it and choose providers and settings that, by those terms, limit retention and training on inputs. As our client base grows, we intend to move to business or developer terms that provide stronger contractual data protections.
  • Support and bug-report forms instruct users not to include Client health information, and we do not need it to resolve most issues. Where Client names or contact details appear in a request and are not needed, we remove or replace them before using an AI tool.
  • Day-to-day software development uses synthetic or de-identified test data, not Client records. During large system updates, we may use AI tools to write and test the code that migrates existing account data to a new structure; in the normal case that code runs on our systems and the Client records themselves are not sent to the AI provider. If a migration requires an AI tool to process actual Client records (for example, to reformat free-text entries), we will limit it to the fields involved, exclude health information unless the provider is bound by a Business Associate Agreement, and note the migration in our release notes.
  • We do not permit any AI service to retain Client PII beyond what its terms require to process the request.

We cannot guarantee how a third-party provider handles data on its own systems, and we do not promise that no AI system will ever process your information. We do promise that we will not sell it, will not provide it for training, and will keep the amount that reaches any AI tool to the minimum needed to help you.

Subscribers control how their Clients' information is used within the Service. A Subscriber may, for example, choose to send a Client marketing messages; that choice is the Subscriber's, governed by the Subscriber's own privacy notice, and KinesioCal only transmits it.

5. When We Share Information

We share personal information only in these cases:

Service providers (subprocessors). Companies that host or support the Service under contracts that restrict them to our instructions and require appropriate security. Our current subprocessors are: payment processing (Stripe); travel-time and address lookup (Valhalla on OpenStreetMap data, run on our own systems; Google Routes, Geoapify, or LocationIQ for addresses we cannot resolve ourselves — they receive addresses only, never a Client's name); Google Calendar when a Subscriber connects its own calendar (the appointment time, service name, and Client name are written to that Subscriber's calendar); and the cloud hosting, email delivery, and error-monitoring providers we select before launch, which we will name here when chosen. We do not send text messages and use no SMS provider. We will update the list before adding a subprocessor that handles Client data.

The Subscriber you booked with. Client information is always visible to the Subscriber that collected it and to the Users that Subscriber authorizes.

Another Subscriber, at the Client's direction. A Client who has records with two or more Subscribers may, from their own account, give one of them read-only access to parts of the record another holds about them: contact details, booking-form answers, appointment history, or the notes that Subscriber marked as shared with the Client. Staff-only notes are never included. Each Subscriber keeps its own record; nothing is changed or merged, the receiving Subscriber sees the information in a separate view labeled as shared by the Client, and the Client can stop the share at any time, after which the receiving Subscriber no longer sees it. Only the Client can create a share; a Subscriber cannot share a Client's record with another Subscriber or request one. Each share and each revocation is recorded in both Subscribers' activity logs, with what was shared and when.

Law enforcement, licensing boards, and legal process. We disclose information to government agencies only as described in Section 5 of our Terms of Service: in response to valid legal process served on KinesioCal, LLC; to prevent imminent death or serious injury; or when we report an account we have a good-faith belief is being used for trafficking, sexual services, or services involving minors. We notify affected Subscribers of requests unless prohibited or unsafe to do so.

The Safety Network. Subscribers may block a Client and share that block with other participating Subscribers under one or more categories: no-call no-show, sexual harassment, threats or violence, unsafe dwelling, policy violation, non-payment, theft, maltreatment of staff, or other. A share also records whether the conduct was a single offense or repeated behavior and whether supporting documentation is on file. Participation is each Subscriber's choice, and a participating Subscriber is matched only with other participating Subscribers within the alert radius it sets around its own location (25 miles unless it changes it, between 1 and 500). The Client's email address and phone number are stored as a one-way hash for matching; the original values are encrypted and readable only by the Subscriber that shared the block and by KinesioCal moderation. No block information is sent to any other Subscriber until the blocked Client attempts to book with a participating Subscriber in range using the same email address or phone number. At that point the receiving Subscriber's log records the categories, single or repeated, whether documentation exists, the date, and any different name or contact details used in the attempt. The receiving Subscriber never sees the identity of the sharing Subscriber, its notes, or its documentation. The attempt is refused, and the Client shown a generic unavailability message, only if the receiving Subscriber has chosen to import that category (and, for a share with no documentation, has chosen to import undocumented shares); otherwise the booking goes ahead and the match is only logged. A refused Client is added to the receiving Subscriber's own blocklist, which that Subscriber controls and can remove at any time. Shares in the sexual harassment and threats or violence categories remain until the sharing Subscriber withdraws them or a review removes them; shares in every other category stop reaching other Subscribers one year after filing unless the sharing Subscriber deliberately renews them. Clients may ask KinesioCal to review a network share as described in the Client Terms of Use. Safety Network data, including block records, categories, and any documentation a business attaches, may be shared with law enforcement and with professional licensing or regulatory boards, either in response to legal process or when we report suspected sexual solicitation, trafficking, threats, assault, or services involving minors. Individual Safety Network records are never sold or published and are not shared with anyone else outside participating Subscribers. We may publish de-identified, aggregated statistics drawn from the Safety Network, such as the number of blocks shared by category, region, or time period, or the rate at which challenges succeed, to inform the profession and the public about practitioner safety. Published statistics will never identify a Client, a business, or a practitioner, and we will suppress any figure small enough that an individual could reasonably be inferred from it.

Ban enforcement. When a person is banned from the platform — a Client under the Client Terms, or the owners and principals of a Subscriber terminated under the Terms of Service — we keep hashed versions of the email address and phone number associated with the banned account, by default for five years and longer where the conduct warrants it, solely to recognise attempts to create a new account or book under new details to get around the ban. We keep no readable copy of those details for this purpose, and the hashes are not used for anything else.

Business transfers. If KinesioCal is acquired, merges, or sells substantially all of its assets, personal information will transfer to the successor as part of that transaction, subject to this Privacy Policy as it stands on the date of transfer. A successor may later change the policy, but only by posting a revised policy and giving the notice described in Section 7. We will notify Subscribers by email at least 30 days before any transfer closes, and Subscribers may export their data and close their account before that date if they do not want their data to transfer. We cannot promise what a successor will do after the transfer, which is why we give you time to leave first.

With your direction. When you ask us to share information, for example by exporting your records, downloading a report, or connecting an integration. A Subscriber's Client records are the Subscriber's business assets, and Subscribers may download them at any time. Once information leaves the Service at your direction, whether by export, download, email, integration, or any other route you initiate, it is outside our systems and our control, and this Privacy Policy and our security safeguards no longer apply to that copy. You are responsible for how you store, protect, and use it, including any notice to Clients and any breach-notification duty that attaches to it under your own licensing rules or state law.

6. Security, Retention, and Deletion

Security. We use the safeguards described in Section 2, plus automatic session timeouts, and regular dependency and vulnerability updates. No system is perfectly secure; if we learn of a breach affecting your information, we will notify affected Subscribers promptly, and within the time state law requires, with the information they need to meet their own obligations: what happened, which Clients and data fields were affected, when, and what we have done in response. For the business's copy of Client data, Subscribers are responsible for notifying their own Clients and regulators as their licensing rules and state law require; KinesioCal does not send those notices on a Subscriber's behalf. For Clients who hold a KinesioCal account, KinesioCal will notify those Clients directly, within the time state law requires, of any breach affecting their account or their own copy of their records.

Retention for Subscribers. We keep a Subscriber's data for as long as its account is active, with two exceptions. Archiving: what a business needs to work today is never archived (Client profiles, notes, and consents of an active account, and its services, retail, rooms, staff, and settings). Past activity that is not needed to function today (logs, past appointments and transactions, used-up commerce) is moved to archive 18 to 24 months after its date, depending on record type (for example, an appointment is measured from the appointment date). Archived records can be retrieved on request to support, but every record may be permanently deleted 30 months after its date, regardless of when it was last viewed or retrieved. Viewing or requesting a copy of a record does not reset or extend this period, and we do not promise to keep any record beyond 30 months from its date. Closed and unpaid accounts: if a Subscriber cancels or closes its account from Settings, it keeps full access until the end of the billing period it has paid for, and its account is then closed. If a Subscriber stops paying, it has a 3-day grace period during which it can still use the portal; after that, portal access is limited to a page where it can reactivate its subscription at any time. In either case, for 30 days from the day access ended, the business may download a complete export of its records, including Client records, from Settings → Downloads, or obtain one by contacting support at KinesioCalendar@gmail.com. After that, we delete the account's data from production systems, after emailing the account's owners, and backups age out on their normal cycle. Deletion covers everything the business held, including its financial and consent records, and removes the logins of staff who belonged only to that business; a Client's own account is unaffected (Section 7), and Safety Network records remain. Reactivating an unpaid account, or reopening a closed one from Settings, before deletion restores access to the data that remains. We may retain records longer where required for legal holds, Safety Network records, tax and financial records, ongoing investigations, or accounts terminated for prohibited use.

Record-retention rules are the Subscriber's responsibility. State licensing boards require practitioners to keep client records for set periods, often several years. KinesioCal is not the custodian of those records for that purpose and does not retain them on a Subscriber's behalf beyond the export window above. Subscribers must export and keep their own copies to meet those rules.

Client accounts are independent of businesses. A Client who creates a KinesioCal account owns that account. It is not tied to any one business: a Client may book with several businesses from one account, and if a business closes or deletes its KinesioCal account, the Client's login and contact details remain until the Client closes the account. A business's copy of a Client's records (intake answers, treatment notes, appointment history with that business) belongs to the business and is deleted or archived with the business's account as described above.

Client deletion requests. Because a Client's information may exist in two places, deletion takes two steps. (1) To delete the records a business holds about you, contact that business; it owns those records and may be legally required to keep some of them for a set period. KinesioCal does not alter or erase a business's records at a Client's request. (2) To close your own KinesioCal account, use Close my account in your portal profile; your login and the contact details held on your account are removed when you confirm, except for Safety Network records and records we must keep by law. Closing your account does not remove the record held by any business you booked with, which remains that business's record of you until the business deletes it or closes; you become a guest client of each business again. We may also delete a Client account that was created but never used to complete a booking 90 days after creation. A Client account with no activity for 24 months may have its login deactivated, after we attempt to email the account holder; the Client reverts to a guest, the records each Subscriber holds about them are unchanged, and they may create a new login at any time. Activity means any action on the account or its records by the Client or a Subscriber, including a booking, charge, sign-in, or record change. If you never created a KinesioCal account and booked only as a guest, you exist in the Service only as a record held by the business, and the business deleting your Client profile removes your contact details, intake answers, notes, and flags from the Service; the business's appointment and payment history keeps an entry without your details, as its books require.

Backups. Backups exist for disaster recovery. They are encrypted and are not a substitute for a Subscriber's own records.

7. Your Rights and Choices

Subscribers and Users may view and correct their account information in Settings, export the business's records from Settings at any time, and close the business's account from Settings; a closed account's records are deleted after the 30-day export window in Section 6. A staff member's login is removed by the business owner, or on request to KinesioCalendar@gmail.com. You may opt out of product-update emails via the unsubscribe link; transactional emails (receipts, security notices) cannot be opted out of while the account is active.

Clients may unsubscribe from a business's marketing emails using the link in any of them; we send email only, never text messages. A business's newsletters and announcements are on for you by default; turn them off at any time under Notifications in your portal, and the setting applies at every business you book with. Turning them off never affects appointment confirmations, reminders, or receipts. If you hold a KinesioCal account, you may view and correct the contact details on your account, export a copy of your records at each business you booked with, and close your account, all from your portal profile. For the copy of your records a business holds, contact that business; it owns that copy and may be required to keep it, and we will support it in responding. If you cannot reach the business, email KinesioCalendar@gmail.com and we will relay your request.

State privacy laws. Depending on where you live, you may have additional rights to know, delete, correct, or limit use of your personal information, and the right not to be discriminated against for exercising them. We honor these rights where they apply.

Children. The Service is not directed to children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect their information directly. A parent or guardian may hold a client account and book for their minor child under the parent's or guardian's own name. The Subscriber the child visits is responsible for the child's record and for obtaining the guardian's consent; the Service gives every Subscriber a Parent/guardian consent form it can send to the parent or replace with its own. Separate accounts for minors linked to a guardian are not offered today.

Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control. We do not respond to browser Do Not Track signals because we do not track users across third-party sites. A Global Privacy Control signal asks us not to sell or share your personal information; we never do, so the signal changes nothing about how we treat you.

Changes. We will post changes here with a new "last updated" date and notify Subscribers by email of material changes at least 30 days before they take effect.
